title: Navigation API: deferring scroll until intercept promise settles

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

It looks as through Chrome waits to [#restore-scroll-position-data](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#restore-scroll-position-data) until the intercept promise resolves, but this isn't specced anywhere. It is however outlined in various tests including - I believe - https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/navigation-api/scroll-behavior/manual-scroll-after-dispatch.html. 

Please correct me if I'm wrong on this, but that looks like what's happening to me. Scroll position is not restored until `back_promises.finished` is finalised. I had a little trouble finding where this happens in Chrome's code, but Chrome's equivalent of restore-scroll-position-data eventually calls to [`SetPendingHistoryRestoreScrollOffset`](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/scroll/scrollable_area.h;drc=1fb4c56b03b105b03c45627871b15b8933ed8a11;l=147) which appears to be applied by other means (it seems as though [`ApplyScrollRestorationLogic()`](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/dom/document.h;l=2019;drc=1fb4c56b03b105b03c45627871b15b8933ed8a11) will apply a pending history scroll offset, and that's called from multiple places including, I believe, View Transitions?).

If this is the case, I propose we add these additional mechanics to the https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#restore-scroll-position-data spec. It _seems_ somewhat trivial to spec this?
